subject: Post-call: data protection & BYO-key qualification for Cardinal Labs
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Morales <lena.morales@cardinallabs.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-14T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — data protection & BYO-key qualification

Hi Lena,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call with Cardinal Labs and the key open items so we can align internal resources:

- SOC 2 / HIPAA posture: you mentioned needing SOC 2 Type II evidence for the inference platform and a HIPAA BA agreement. We can provide our most recent SOC 2 report (2026) and a draft BA for your legal team.
- Key model: you prefer a customer-managed keys approach (BYO-key) with FIPS-compliant HSM. We discussed two integration options: (A) CloudHSM-backed customer key material managed via a KMIP-compatible gateway; (B) on-prem HSM connector that establishes an encrypted tunnel to Redwood's control plane and stores only key handles.
- Data flows: at-rest encryption will use per-tenant DEKs wrapped by the customer's KEKs; in-transit is TLS 1.3 with mTLS option for private deployments.

Attachments: attaching the brief architecture sketch we referenced (redwood-byo-architecture.png) and our standard security snapshot (security-snapshot-2027.pdf).

Next steps / asks:
1) Could you confirm the Cardinal Labs HSM vendor (CloudHSM, Thales, or vendor name) and whether you require key exportability?
2) We'll loop in Neha (security) to answer detailed questionnaire items — expect a short intake from her within 48 hours.
3) If you want, we can schedule a 45-minute BYO-key integration demo + technical Q&A next week.

I'll draft a mutual action plan once we have your answers to (1).

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-byo-architecture.png, security-snapshot-2027.pdf
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Morales <lena.morales@cardinallabs.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-14T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — data protection & BYO-key qualification

Hi Lena — great to meet you over video earlier.

High-level answers to the most pressing items you raised:

- SOC 2 / HIPAA: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II for our core inference and control plane in Q4 2026. We're HIPAA-ready for customers under a Business Associate Agreement; our BA is standard but we can negotiate narrow scopes if needed.
- BYO-key options: both integration patterns Jordan listed are supported. Our recommended path for Cardinal Labs (given the need for HSM-backed keys) is using a CloudHSM or Thales HSM where KEKs remain in your control; Redwood only stores non-sensitive key handles and never the raw KEK material. We support KMIP and vendor-specific APIs (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM, Thales Luna).
- Key rotation & recovery: DEKs rotate on a configurable cadence; KEK rotation is driven by your KMS/HSM policy. For disaster recovery we support split-key escrow through a third-party key escrow provider if you require non-exportable keys with recovery guarantees.
- Audit & logs: we provide KMS usage logs, per-request token traces, and can integrate with your SIEM over syslog/s3.

I attached a short intake spreadsheet to capture Cardinal Labs' current KMS/HSM footprint, compliance deadlines, and any non-negotiable controls (CardinalLabs-security-questionnaire-filled.xlsx). Please fill the shaded fields when convenient.

I can also run a short technical session with our SRE engineers to walk through the connector and crypto flows; propose Tue/Wed next week.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: CardinalLabs-security-questionnaire-filled.xlsx
From: Lena Morales <lena.morales@cardinallabs.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-15T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — data protection & BYO-key qualification

Thanks Jordan and Neha — this is helpful.

A few quick clarifications from our side before we fill the intake workbook:

- HSM vendor: we currently run Thales Luna on-prem and are evaluating a CloudHSM failover. Our security team does not allow key export by default; we need clear documentation on whether Redwood requires any key material import/export.
- Split-key escrow: can you outline third-party providers you've worked with (for contractual references)? Our legal will want references.
- Timeline: our compliance board reviews new vendors on 3/29. If we can get the questionnaire back completed and a short POC plan before 3/24, we can put Redwood on the board for approval.

I've attached a short baseline vendor questionnaire with our fields pre-populated (CardinalLabs-security-questionnaire-filled.xlsx). Note the sections on FIPS level and HSM tamper-resistance — those are gating items.

We'll aim to have the filled intake workbook back to you by EOD 3/17.

Best,
Lena Morales
Head of IT Risk | Cardinal Labs

Attachments: CardinalLabs-security-questionnaire-filled.xlsx
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-16T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap — data protection & BYO-key qualification

Looping up next steps after Lena's note. Key actions for our side:

- Neha: please draft a concise one-page note on our BYO integration that explicitly states we do not require KEK export/import and lists supported HSM vendors and FIPS levels. Include two customer references if possible.
- Monica: prepare a high-level POC plan (3 sprints) and a rough cost estimate for a dedicated connector + SRE support. Cardinal Labs is asking for a POC plan before 3/24.
- I'll propose and send 3 possible time slots for a 45-min technical demo to Lena and her team (aiming for next Tue/Wed).

Deal: DL-2028-0927 — potential midsize healthcare/diagnostics account; timeline aligned to Cardinal's compliance board on 3/29.

Thanks — Jordan
